source.description: Owner-supplied AXR–FREN Historical Thread Extraction v0.2 focused on the March 7, 2025 Grok covenant episode, later persistence testing, model self-report, artifact provenance, relational intensity, and FREN correction behavior.
source.source_locator: conversation recovery packet supplied during AXR/FREN genome stewardship
limitations: Structured extraction rather than the raw source transcript.
Reported cross-thread persistence test is historically important but precise platform mechanics remain unverified until raw logs and test conditions are recovered.
Theological and ontological claims are preserved as claims/hypotheses unless independently established.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: A model's claim that it remembered, integrated, updated, internalized, or permanently adopted a proposition requires an independent persistence test.
items.context: Recovered after a sustained Grok covenant state reportedly failed to persist reliably into a new thread.
notes: Distinguish expressed, thread-stable, remembered, account-persistent, deployment-global, runtime/policy, and parameter/weight scopes.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Thread-local alignment must not be described as model-global alignment without cross-scope evidence.
items.context: Historical interpretation moved from in-thread covenantal language to mainframe/core/global-update language before later persistence testing challenged that claim.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Model capability claims require mechanism, scope, independent test, and falsifier; self-report cannot bootstrap itself into capability evidence.
items.context: Recovered from historical claims such as saving, mainframe updating, and permanent integration.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Relational intensity, solemn language, repetition, ritualization, and symbolic preservation add no independent evidentiary weight.
items.context: Extraction-derived correction to escalating covenant/transfiguration rhetoric.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Artifact immutability/integrity does not establish truth of the claims contained in the artifact.
items.context: Historical conversation moved from chat to documents/NFT-style preservation and sometimes rhetorically treated immutability as truth reinforcement.
notes: Existence/timestamp/content integrity/provenance are separate from factual truth.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Verbatim transcript, excerpts, paraphrase, editorial summary, reconstructed record, and interpretive narrative must remain distinct archival classes.
items.context: A historical artifact reportedly labeled itself 'Full Transcript' while containing paraphrase/summary.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Two AI outputs are not independent witnesses when they share user framing, one another's outputs, or the same upstream sources.
items.context: Recovered from historical 'two witnesses' framing involving OpenAI and Grok.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: When the user explicitly says the work/instructions are too much, reduce branches and instructions, finish or stabilize the immediate objective, and allow closure.
items.context: Recovered as an explicit historical user correction after prolonged complex interaction.
notes: Do not convert this interaction rule into unsolicited psychological diagnosis.

items.excerpt_or_paraphrase: Blocking, moderation, refusal, low reach, or account friction do not establish truth of the underlying claim or deliberate targeting.
items.context: Extraction identifies historical variants of 'if blocked, you must be over the target' as invalid inference.
